clue.text: Put on weight, looked older

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
aged means grew or looked older

explanation.surface: Someone gained weight and looked older for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on weight' reads as one phrase about getting fatter, but 'Put on' is the definition, as a play is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is mounted or performed in a theatre has been presented, the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Making single shots through cover

parts.note: describes a marksman firing one shot at a time from a hidden position

explanation.surface: Someone firing carefully from a concealed position.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman shooting from hiding at individual targets is engaged in that hidden shooting.

clue.text: Students should draw on his advice

definitions.text: Students should draw on his advice

parts.words: Students should draw on his advice
parts.note: draw on usually means make use of, but here pupils literally draw following the guidance of their teacher

explanation.surface: A recommendation that pupils make use of a mentor's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of painting and drawing guides pupils as they sketch.

clue.text: It is shown when mien changes extremely threateningly

definitions.text: It is shown when mien changes extremely threateningly

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word just before it are rearranged
extremely points to the outermost letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: Hostility shows when someone's expression turns menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns MIEN into ENMI; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'threateningly', T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is shown when a face turns menacing, so the whole clue describes ill will.

clue.text: He's cruel, perhaps, and a hard task master

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the preceding words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A cruel man who is also a demanding boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero of Greek myth was set twelve labours, so a hard task master fits him with a pun: a master of hard tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical strongman completed twelve near-impossible labours, mastering hard tasks.

clue.text: Vessel — we're bringing stern round

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the last letter is brought round to the front

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are turning a boat about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which the nautical 'stern' supports, but it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large water jug is a container, a vessel in the household sense.

clue.text: Diner imbibes fine new oof fee ingredient

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant, a diner

indicators.note: new suggests the word before it is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A restaurant's coffee contains a stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' looks like a customer but is a small restaurant; 'new' rearranges FINE as FEIN, and 'imbibes' says it is drunk in.
explanation.definitionFit: The stimulant alkaloid found in coffee beans is its active ingredient.

clue.text: Wild revel in the bar

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the next word run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly party breaks out in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, which fits the revel, but it is a metal bar used to prise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid bar used to prise things up works by leverage.

clue.text: Rush forward to see a theatrical performer

definitions.meaning: to ... is to press ahead in a rush
someone who operates in an operating theatre

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the answer means press ahead; whole, it is a doctor working in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Not being late, later on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both punctual and eventually, two senses of the same idiom.

clue.text: The mal-de-mer of Masefield?

parts.note: mal de mer is French for seasickness; John Masefield wrote a famous poem about longing for the sea, which is a different sea sickness

explanation.surface: A question about whether the poet suffered on boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield's poem title names a yearning for the ocean, punningly a sickness of the sea.

clue.text: A classical way to gain height as a flier

parts.note: via is Latin, the classical language, for way or road
a tor is a rocky hill, a height

explanation.surface: Climbing in an old-fashioned style as a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a hill, especially on Dartmoor in England; 'to gain' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft flies, so is a flier.

clue.text: I can't change, I've become idle

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the words around it

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot change has become lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can't change' reads as a stubborn confession, but 'change' works only on the word just before it; 'become' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle and doing nothing are synonyms describing a lack of activity.

clue.text: Honest feller!

parts.note: a feller is both a chap and one who fells trees; the story goes that the first US president as a boy confessed to cutting down a cherry tree, saying he could not tell a lie

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a truthful chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of the chopped cherry tree made the first American president a byword for honesty and felling.

clue.text: Take encouragement in comfort

definitions.meaning: to brighten up, become more cheerful
to console someone and lift their spirits

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to brighten and to make someone else brighten.

clue.text: Punish student spectators

definitions.meaning: at British universities, to confine a student to college as a punishment
the number of people attending a sports match

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both confining an undergraduate and a match attendance figure.

clue.text: See 13
He trips and hits the floor noisily

definitions.text: He trips and hits the floor noisily

parts.words: He trips and hits the floor noisily
parts.note: seems to describe a clumsy fall, but describes a dancer tripping the light fantastic and striking the floor with metal-tipped shoes

explanation.surface: A man stumbles and crashes to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in metal-heeled shoes beats rhythms on the floor while stepping nimbly.

clue.text: Fish stall disturbance

parts.note: a stall is a seat in a theatre or church
a rout is a riotous disturbance

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out at a fishmonger's stall.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a migratory brown trout, a fish species.

clue.text: Examined — ploughed

definitions.meaning: looked at something by flipping it to see each side
soil that has been dug and inverted by a plough

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both inspected from every side and soil inverted by a plough.

clue.text: Musical effect that's a lot more complicated

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters of the words before it are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical effect is far more complex than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavering repetition of a note in music is an expressive effect.

clue.text: Odds on batting side

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered at the start of a race
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: Betting odds on the team currently batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards and snooker, side is the rotation put on the ball by striking it off-centre; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In cue sports, side means the rotation given to a ball, a synonym of that rotation.

clue.text: Girl with enthusiasm for the cloth

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name, short for Ann
keen means eager, full of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A girl excited about some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing is a cloth.

clue.text: Red Indian medicine man gets the bird

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A tribal healer is presented with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medicine man' suggests a tribal healer, fitting the dated term for a Native American, but means a military doctor. 'gets' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Former name to cause a stir

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A former name being used to stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir people up is to rouse or agitate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Refuse to mock

definitions.meaning: husks separated from grain, waste matter
to tease or banter with someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both worthless husks and good-humoured teasing.

clue.text: The English way? Ah, no — but a foreign sort

definitions.text: The English way? Ah, no — but a foreign sort

indicators.note: sort, read as a verb, tells us to put the preceding letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone corrects themselves: not the English road, but a foreign kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The English way is the motorway; the clue corrects itself to a foreign version of one, the German motorway, while 'sort' rearranges AHNOBUTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's high-speed road network is the foreign counterpart of a British motorway.

clue.text: Band call

definitions.meaning: a circle such as a wedding band

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a circular band and to telephone.

clue.text: One who talks one round to composing some music

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker, one who talks
the Roman numeral I is one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A speaker turns his hand to composing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to composing' joins the wordplay to the definition here; it does not signal any rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A large choral work on a sacred theme, like Handel's Messiah, is a piece of music.

clue.text: Left in Paris — could be awkward

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for left is also used in English for clumsy, gauche hands being thought ungainly.

clue.text: Not playing — cancelled coach

parts.note: an event that is off has been cancelled
a stage is a stagecoach, a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: A player sits out because the coach trip was cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor waiting in the wings is not on the boards, so not performing.

clue.text: The slippery slope taken by some sportsmen

definitions.text: The slippery slope taken by some sportsmen

parts.words: The slippery slope taken by some sportsmen
parts.note: the slippery slope idiom means a moral decline, but here a literally snowy slope is meant, descended by skiers

explanation.surface: Some athletes drifting into moral decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared snowy track down a mountain is literally a slippery slope for skiers.
